clue.text: Make a meal of school subject, getting tense

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject
the past is a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: A pupil makes a fuss over a lesson that has turned stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a meal of' reads as an idiom for overdoing something; only 'a meal' is the definition. RE is religious education, a subject in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal or literary word for a meal or feast.

clue.text: Most neglected sites being restored — there's excitement about that

indicators.note: about tells us the excitement word goes round the rearranged sites

parts.note: rut is the sexual excitement of deer and other animals in season

indicators.note: being restored suggests the sites are put back together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Run-down historic sites are being renovated, and people are thrilled about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being restored' gives STIES. 'excitement' sounds like public enthusiasm, but it is the rut, the mating season of deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Things left neglected corrode and decay, so the most neglected are the most corroded, a superlative to match a superlative.

clue.text: Climbing mountain with stick in work for business agency?

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
to cement is to stick things together

explanation.surface: A mountaineer with a walking stick at work, oddly asking about an agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns ALP into PLA, written upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Employment agencies arrange job postings for clients, and such a posting is the work they find.

clue.text: Length of timber, as you might say, put on vehicle in wood?

indicators.note: as you might say tells us the timber word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a sill is a length of timber forming the base of a window or door frame
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A carpenter loads a plank onto a van parked among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as you might say' gives SYL for SILL; 'put on' places it above VAN in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvan describes things belonging to or found among woods and forests, so 'in wood' is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: Biased worker going after power

indicators.note: going after means the worker word follows the power letter

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: A prejudiced employee chases influence.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan view is one-sided, favouring one party or cause.

clue.text: English cant — it jars in writer who is supposed to guarantee quality

definitions.text: who is supposed to guarantee quality

indicators.note: in says the shaken letters sit inside the writer word

parts.note: an author is a writer

indicators.note: jars means jolts or shakes, so these letters are jolted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hypocritical English talk grates on a writer meant to vouch for quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jars' looks like a verb about grating on the ear, but it shakes the letters into ENTICAT; 'in' then sets them inside the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who authenticates verifies that a thing is genuine, vouching for its quality.

clue.text: Cry in country from fellow coming in hot, disturbed

indicators.note: coming in says the fellow word enters the other letters
disturbed means the letters of hot are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: an ally is a fellow or comrade

explanation.surface: Someone in the countryside shouts as a companion arrives flustered and overheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' gives THO, and 'coming in' splits it. 'Cry in country' means a rural shout: the call of the British fox-hunting field.
explanation.definitionFit: A huntsman's shout on sighting the fox is a traditional rural call in the hunting field.

clue.text: Search part of this courtyard

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Look through a section of this enclosed yard.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour an area is to search it thoroughly.

clue.text: International organisation upset over ruler bombing

indicators.note: over means the first piece sits above the ruler in this down entry
upset in a down entry means the letters are turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: The United Nations is in turmoil over a monarch who has launched air raids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns UN into NU; 'over' sets it above KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Attacking with nuclear weapons is a form of bombing, and the slang verb covers bombing generally.

clue.text: Stop everybody on the street

indicators.note: on means the everybody word comes next to, after, the street letters

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Halt every person out in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A car or engine that stalls comes to a stop; to stall also means to halt progress.

clue.text: First person to converse about line making comeback in a particular craft

parts.note: me is the first-person pronoun

indicators.note: about says the talk word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to talk is to converse

indicators.note: making comeback means the line word comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a row is a line

explanation.surface: A first speaker chats about a queue returning, all within a craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' gives WOR and 'about' wraps the conversing word round it; 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Working with metal to make objects is a recognised handicraft taught in schools.

clue.text: New terms chemists used in German company

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: Chemists working for a German firm adopt fresh terminology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges TERMS CHEMISTS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Messerschmitt was a German aircraft manufacturer, famous for its wartime fighter planes.

clue.text: Area cold, one to the west, showing frozen extremities

indicators.note: to the west means the letters travel leftwards, read backwards in an across entry

parts.note: a space is an area
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cold region to the west has frostbitten fingers and toes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the west' reads SPACE, C and I right to left. 'frozen extremities' suggests frostbite but means polar ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar ice sheets cover the planet's extreme ends, frozen at top and bottom.

clue.text: See extremity of aircraft with man on wing

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: extremity of points to the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: Watch the tip of a plane as a pilot stands on its wing.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY is the crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An elytron is the hardened forewing of a beetle, serving as a wing case.

clue.text: Observed only part of play in auditorium

indicators.note: in auditorium means as heard by the audience, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a scene is just one part of a play

explanation.surface: An audience watched just a fragment of a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen is the past participle of see, so it means watched or observed.

clue.text: In business, hassle and shine to a great degree?

definitions.meaning: to haggle a seller into lowering a price
what a fierce sun does, blazing on everything below

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is how strong sunshine is described: the sun is said to blaze downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggling a price lower and blazing sunshine are both described by this two-word phrasal verb.

clue.text: Youth not blossoming into manhood

parts.note: the mythical beautiful youth who never grew up but was turned into a flower

explanation.walkthrough: 'blossoming into manhood' sounds like maturing, but in the Greek myth the young man literally blossomed, becoming a flower instead of a man.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the vain young man died gazing at his reflection and became the daffodil-like flower.

clue.text: Stir food that's hot?

definitions.meaning: slang for prison or a prison sentence
an oat dish served warm at breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: Both 'stir' and the answer are British slang for jail time; 'Stir' reads as a cooking verb to hide this.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal cooked in milk or water is eaten hot, and the word is also British slang for time served in jail.

clue.text: After proper preparation can start to perform

indicators.note: after proper preparation suggests the letters have been reorganised before use

explanation.surface: Once you have prepared well, you are ready to begin your performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After proper preparation' rearranges CAN START.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to carry it out, i.e. to conduct or perform it.

clue.text: Upset produced by a fool, female troublemaker

parts.note: git is British slang for a fool
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Distress caused by a foolish man and a mischievous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: GIT is British slang for an idiot; ATE is the Greek goddess of folly and strife.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate someone is to disturb or stir them up emotionally.

clue.text: Three in inadequate attempt against ten

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the attempt word loses its last letter

parts.note: a try is an attempt
ten is written in digits as 1 and 0, read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A trio forms from a poor attempt against a team of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' cuts TRY to TR; 'against' just places IO alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three, especially musicians.

clue.text: Children housed by Indians in special facility for tots

indicators.note: housed by says the children letters go inside the Indians word

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: Native American children are cared for in a special nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the dictionary abbreviation for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A creche is a nursery where young children are looked after while parents work or shop.

clue.text: At end of journey the French drink (no small amount!)

indicators.note: at end of means the French word comes after the journey word

parts.note: a trip is a journey
le is French for the

explanation.surface: After a trip, a French traveller downs a hefty drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A triple is a drink with three measures of spirit, hence far from a small amount.

clue.text: Bunk that may go into a skip

definitions.text: that may go into a skip
definitions.meaning: waste thrown into a skip, a large open British builder's bin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a bed but means nonsense; a skip is a large open waste container left in British streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense and refuse share this word: both are trash, one spoken and one thrown out.

clue.text: Article removed from chest in port

indicators.note: removed means the article is taken out of the chest word

parts.note: the breast is the chest
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item is taken from a trunk in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' looks like a box, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Brest is a naval port in Brittany, north-west France.

clue.text: Dog to go off course — there's row about that

indicators.note: about says the row word goes round the straying word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to stray or go off course

explanation.surface: A dog strays from its path and there is a quarrel over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel, but it is a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed type of small, lively dog, bred for hunting vermin.

clue.text: French gentleman crashing a vehicle by river

indicators.note: crashing suggests the words are smashed up and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A French gent crashes a car beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' rearranges A VEHICLE; R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevalier is a French knight or cavalier, a gentleman of rank.

clue.text: Sitting pretty?

parts.note: a model holding an attractive position for an artist or camera

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sitting pretty' is an idiom for being comfortable, but read literally it describes a model sitting attractively for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: A model who holds an attractive stance for a painter or photographer has done exactly this.

clue.text: Request to take food into vestibule?

indicators.note: into says the food word is put inside the vestibule word

parts.note: an entry is an entrance hall or vestibule
to eat is to take food

explanation.surface: Asking whether one may eat a meal in the hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or appeal.

clue.text: One dealing with a letter wanting money periodically

definitions.text: One dealing with a letter wanting money periodically

parts.words: One dealing with a letter wanting money periodically
parts.note: a tenant who deals with a landlord, one who lets property and wants rent at intervals

explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests a written letter, but here it is one who lets property, a landlord who wants rent regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant holding a lease deals with the landlord and pays them rent at regular intervals.
